# Prismata Cognitive Feedback Loop Specification

Last updated: 2026-06-01

Version: 0.1.0

(BE / WHEN / WHEN‑NOT / DO / HOW / WHERE)

Code
# Prismata Cognitive Identity & Duty‑Cycle Model
version: 1.0.0
status: evolving
⭐ 1. Overview
Prismata’s cognition is governed by a dual‑layer identity engine:

BE — what a project is

DO — what a project does

These two layers form a cybernetic loop, continuously shaping and reshaping each other.

Inside BE live the activation and inhibition systems:

WHEN — activation

WHEN‑NOT — inhibition

Inside DO live the realization systems:

Implementational HOW — how behavior is physically realized

WHERE — where the implementation lives

Together, these form Prismata’s cognitive feedback and duty‑cycling engine.

🧠 2. BE — Ontological Identity
Code
be:
  identity:
    id:
    name:
    version:
    description:
BE defines:

conceptual identity

semantic role

ontological relationships

emergent meaning

BE contains the ontological HOW:

project_type

project_role

project_interfaces

This is the Mind of the organism.

⏳ 3. WHEN — Activation Layer (Inside BE)
Code
be:
  when:
    temporal:
    triggered:
    emergent:
WHEN defines all conditions under which a project becomes active.

Modes:
Temporal — cron, intervals, windows

Triggered — events, changes, signals

Emergent — readiness, thresholds, organism‑state

WHEN is the activation engine of the organism.

🚫 4. WHEN‑NOT — Inhibition Layer (Inside BE)
Code
be:
  when_not:
    temporal:
    triggered:
    emergent:
WHEN‑NOT defines all conditions under which a project must not activate.

Modes:
Temporal inhibition — blackout windows

Triggered inhibition — failure events, unsafe states

Emergent inhibition — unmet thresholds, conflicting conditions

WHEN‑NOT is the safety and suppression engine.

🧩 5. Ontological HOW (Inside BE)
Code
be:
  how:
    conceptual_structure:
    semantic_relationships:
    identity_composition:
Ontological HOW defines:

how the project exists conceptually

how it fits into the organism’s meaning graph

how its identity is composed

This is the semantic structure of the project.

Guided Link: ontological HOW

⚙️ 6. DO — Behavioral Identity
Code
do:
  capabilities:
  responsibilities:
  workflows:
  interfaces:
DO defines:

what the project does

how it behaves

what it exposes

what it depends on

This is the behavioral expression of identity.

Guided Link: DO layer

🏗️ 7. Implementational HOW (Inside DO)
Code
do:
  how:
    code_structure:
    runtime_architecture:
    module_boundaries:
    dependency_graph:
Implementational HOW defines:

how the project is physically realized

how its code is structured

how its runtime is wired

how its modules interact

This is the Body of the organism.

Guided Link: implementational HOW

📍 8. WHERE — Physical Location (Inside Implementational HOW)
Code
do:
  how:
    where:
      path:
      repo:
      module:
WHERE defines:

where the project lives

where its code resides

where its manifest and schema are located

This is the physical anchor of the project.

Guided Link: WHERE / Index

🔄 9. The Cognitive Feedback Loop
Code
BE → WHEN → DO → HOW → WHERE → WHEN‑NOT → BE
Loop Dynamics:
BE defines identity

WHEN activates potential

DO expresses behavior

Implementational HOW realizes behavior

WHERE anchors behavior

WHEN‑NOT inhibits or halts behavior

BE updates identity

Loop repeats

Guided Link: cognitive loop

This loop is continuous, adaptive, and emergent.

🔁 10. Duty‑Cycling Model
Duty‑cycling is the rhythmic activation and inhibition of projects based on:

WHEN (activation)

WHEN‑NOT (inhibition)

organism state

readiness

dependency health

temporal windows

Duty‑cycling ensures:

stability

efficiency

emergent coordination

self‑regulation

Guided Link: duty cycling

⭐ 11. Summary
Layer	Purpose	Guided Link
BE	Ontological identity	Identity
WHEN	Activation	Activation
WHEN‑NOT	Inhibition	Safety
Ontological HOW	Conceptual structure	Meaning
DO	Behavioral identity	Action
Implementational HOW	Physical realization	Body
WHERE	Physical location	Anchor


This is the Prismata Cognitive Identity Engine.
